name: outsw
synopsis: void outsw(unsigned short port, const void *addr, unsigned long count);
description: outsw performs low-level output of words (16 bits) from a buffer to a specified I/O port. It writes 'count' words starting from the address 'addr' to the port. These functions are primarily for kernel use but can be accessed from user space with proper I/O permissions.

parameters.name: port
parameters.description: The I/O port to write to

parameters.name: addr
parameters.description: Pointer to the buffer containing the data to output

parameters.name: count
parameters.description: The number of words to output

return_value.failure: May cause a segmentation fault if I/O permissions are not set

errors.description: Segmentation fault if the process does not have permission to access the I/O ports

bugs: These functions must be compiled with optimization enabled (-O or -O2 or similar), otherwise they are defined as inline macros and will not be substituted, causing unresolved references at link time.
versions: Hardware-specific; the value argument is passed first and the port argument second, opposite to most DOS implementations.
